To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the development of improved operational seasonal forecasting systems for crop management is a key component of improved management of the whole agricultural value chain.

• Operational seasonal forecasting of crop yield and quality is possible, and is of value to crop producers and other agricultural stakeholders, • The value of seasonal forecasts depends on the skill of the forecast, and the quality of the decision support systems and associated facilitated discussions, •
the integration of seasonal forecasting with agricultural decision making can substantially improve the performance of agricultural enterprises.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following: • Development and evaluation of improved seasonal forecast models and systems for agricultural management • Development and application of decision support tools and associated facilitated discussion systems
the development and evaluation of operational seasonal forecasting systems, linked to decision-support systems, for improved management of crop production systems.
the following key questions: How can the seasonal forecasting system be improved? How can the system be linked more effectively to decision making?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
seasonal forecast systems have considerable value in improving operational decision making in the agricultural sector.

operational seasonal forecasting systems are of value in improving agricultural production, but that this is dependent on the quality and appropriateness of the systems and the extent to which they are integrated with the decision-making process.

operational crop forecasting systems can provide substantial benefits for crop production managers, but that this is not the case unless the forecasting system is linked with appropriate decision support tools, and unless there is an effective process for facilitating the decision-making process.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
seasonal forecasting of crop production performance is now possible and is of considerable operational value.
we have demonstrated that seasonal forecasting of agricultural production is feasible and has potential value in improving management of crop production.

the development of a seasonal forecast system for crop production requires a multidisciplinary approach, where climate, crop growth and agricultural management scientists work together with crop producers to develop the most effective system.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is a need for more research on the development and application of seasonal forecasting systems for agricultural production.
there are many opportunities for improving the performance of agricultural production through the application of seasonal forecasting.
the value of seasonal forecasting is in the application of the information to decision making in agricultural production and marketing, rather than in the forecasting itself.
